How a preset stores its sequence

A preset keeps sequencer patterns A and B at fixed positions after its named parameters. Each pattern holds 64 steps, whatever the sequence length, followed by a short pattern trailer. The length, gate length and smoothing are named parameters that both patterns share.
How a preset stores its sequence

mise run microfreak:inspect FILE --sequence adds the decoded patterns to the inspector's JSON. mise run microfreak:write-sequence writes a sequence description into a preset and uploads it, using lib/sequence.py. Microfreak/Sequence/Write a sequence describes the description format, the tasks and how to check a slot on the instrument.

0–3, notes: one MIDI note per voice. A value of 0x80 or more means no note there; the instrument writes 0xFF, and some factory presets hold 0xFB or 0xFD. The instrument plays voices from voice 1 up to the first empty one: a step whose voice 1 was empty stayed silent with a note in voice 2 or voice 4, and [60, empty, 64, empty] played only 60.
How a preset stores its sequence
4–7, velocities: one per voice, sent as the note's MIDI velocity. Use 1–127. Velocity 0 went out as a note-on with velocity 0, which receivers treat as a note-off. Velocity 200 sent no note-on.
How a preset stores its sequence

8–11, modulation-track values: one per track, 0–255. With smoothing off, track 1 aimed at filter cutoff sent CC 23 at half the stored value on each step that held a value: 0, 32, 64, 128, 192, 255, 10 and 200 went out as 0, 16, 32, 64, 96, 127, 5 and 100.

0–7, modulation-track destinations: four little-endian ids, one per track, FFFF for an unused track. 0x0101 sent CC 23 (filter cutoff) and 0x0602 sent CC 106 (envelope decay). The other ids in the decoder's table come from Freakout's live-parameter map and are untried on my MicroFreak.

8, gate copy: equals the gate length in percent in every preset read, but playback ignores it. With Seq.GateLen at 90% and this value at 20, notes lasted 5 of 6 clocks; with Seq.GateLen at 20% and this value at 90, 1 of 6 clocks. Freakout reports that this value shortened the gate; on my MicroFreak the named parameter decided.

9, length copy: equals the sequence length in every preset read. With Seq.Length at 8 and this value at 16, the pattern looped every 8 steps. Setting it to 0 changed nothing heard. Freakout found the same.

10 and 11: in factory presets, 10 is 0 in A and 1 in B, and 11 is 1 in exactly one of the two patterns. Swapping both between A and B left pattern A playing A's steps, so neither picks the pattern that plays.

I describe a sequence in words, such as "in slot 483, a 16-step minor arpeggio on A with a rest every fourth step, pattern B the same an octave up, accent the downbeats". These steps put it into a preset on my MicroFreak and check that the instrument plays it as described.

Two mise tasks do the work. mise run microfreak:write-sequence writes a description file into a preset and uploads it to a slot. mise run microfreak:verify-sequence does the same write, then plays the slot, records what the MicroFreak sends over MIDI and what the Zoom H5/My Unit hears, downloads the slot again, and reports for every step what the description expects, what the instrument sent and what it sounded.
